title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 66
paragraphs: Meanwhile those appointed to serve in Xerxes's fleet, having observed from Trachis the disaster of the Lacedaemonians and crossed over from there to Histiaia, after staying three days sailed through the Euripos, and in another three days reached Phaleron. As I suppose, they made their attack on Athens with forces, both by land and sea, no fewer than when they had arrived at Sepias and Thermopylae. Against those who perished in the storm and those who fell at Thermopylae and in the sea-fights at Artemisium, I would set those who at that time had not yet been accompanying the king: the Malians, Dorians, Locrians, and Boeotians (who accompanied him as a body, except the Thespians and Plataeans), and moreover the men of Carystos, Andros, and Tenos, with all the other islanders except the five cities I named before. For the further the Persian advanced toward the center of Greece, the more nations joined him.
